rules.quote: It sends and receives bytes on a serial line in 8N1 format. 8N1 framing: one start bit (0), eight data bits with the least significant bit first, no parity, one stop bit (1).
rules.statement: Serial frames use 8N1: one start bit (0), eight data bits least significant bit first, no parity, one stop bit (1).

review.reason: Quote states 8N1 framing exactly.

rules.quote: The bit period is a fixed number of i_clk cycles, set by a parameter. Bit period of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT clock cycles.
rules.statement: Each serial bit period lasts exactly PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT i_clk cycles.

review.reason: Bit period is PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT clocks per quote.

rules.quote: The system side has one valid/ready byte stream for transmit and one for receive. Transmit stream input (i_tx_valid, o_tx_ready, i_tx_data) with a valid/ready handshake.
rules.statement: The transmit stream transfers a byte i_tx_data using a valid/ready handshake on i_tx_valid and o_tx_ready.

review.reason: Transmit valid/ready stream stated.

rules.quote: The system side has one valid/ready byte stream for transmit and one for receive. Receive stream output (o_rx_valid, i_rx_ready, o_rx_data, o_rx_frame_err).
rules.statement: The receive stream delivers each byte o_rx_data with o_rx_frame_err using a valid/ready handshake on o_rx_valid and i_rx_ready.

review.reason: Receive valid/ready stream with frame_err stated.

rules.quote: The line is high when idle.
rules.condition: When the serial line is idle
rules.statement: The serial transmit line is high when idle.

review.reason: Idle high is checkable every cycle only if idle state is known from interface; idle is internal state (o_txd high when no frame in progress). Scenario check is safer; the line-high requirement is observable via bench tracking of tx activity.

rules.quote: The parameter is fixed at elaboration and its legal range is 4 to 65535.
rules.statement: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is fixed at elaboration and its legal range is 4 to 65535.

review.reason: Parameter range stated; exercised via elaboration scenarios, not assertion.

rules.quote: Bytes sent back to back have no idle bit between the stop bit and the next start bit.
rules.condition: When bytes are sent back to back
rules.statement: No idle bit is inserted between the stop bit and the next start bit.

review.reason: Back-to-back bytes have no idle gap; observable on txd.

rules.quote: A one-byte holding register keeps each received byte until it is taken.
rules.condition: After a byte is received until it is taken
rules.statement: A one-byte holding register keeps each received byte until it is taken.

review.reason: Holding register keeps byte until taken; observable via o_rx_valid/o_rx_data stability.

rules.quote: Start-bit detection on a falling edge, a second start-bit check in the middle of the bit (glitch rejection), and sampling of every data bit and the stop bit in the middle of the bit.
rules.statement: Every data bit and the stop bit are sampled in the middle of the bit.

review.reason: Mid-bit sampling of data and stop bits stated.

merged_from.quote: Start-bit detection on a falling edge, a second start-bit check in the middle of the bit (glitch rejection), and sampling of every data bit and the stop bit in the middle of the bit.

rules.quote: A frame error flag (stop bit sampled as 0), delivered together with the byte.
rules.condition: When the stop bit is sampled as 0
rules.statement: o_rx_frame_err is set and delivered together with the received byte.

review.reason: Frame error flag delivered with byte when stop bit is 0.

rules.quote: An overrun pulse (o_rx_overrun) when a received byte is dropped because the previous byte has not been taken.
rules.condition: When a received byte is dropped because the previous byte has not been taken
rules.statement: o_rx_overrun pulses.

review.reason: Overrun pulse on dropped byte stated.

rules.quote: Full duplex: the transmitter and the receiver work at the same time and do not depend on each other.
rules.statement: The transmitter and receiver operate simultaneously and independently of each other (full duplex).

review.reason: Full duplex independence stated.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT; Default: 16; Legal values: 4 to 65535; Description: Bit period in i_clk cycles (N), used by the transmitter and the receiver
rules.statement: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT (default 16, legal 4 to 65535) defines the bit period N in i_clk cycles used by both transmitter and receiver.

review.reason: Quote defines the parameter, default, legal range and use by both TX and RX; exercised by scenarios with different values.

rules.quote: Parameter: LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT; Default: Derived; Legal values: -; Description: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT / 2 with integer division (floor); the middle-of-bit sampling offset H [REQ-PAR-002] LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT shall equal floor(PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT / 2).
rules.statement: LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT shall equal floor(PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT / 2), the middle-of-bit sampling offset H, using integer division.

review.reason: REQ-PAR-002 states HALF_BIT = floor(N/2) explicitly; verifiable by sampling-point scenarios with odd and even N.

rules.quote: [REQ-PAR-001] The block shall behave as specified for every value of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT from 4 to 65535 inclusive, both odd and even.
rules.condition: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is any value from 4 to 65535 inclusive, odd or even
rules.statement: The block shall behave as specified for every PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT value from 4 to 65535 inclusive, both odd and even.

review.reason: REQ-PAR-001 explicitly requires correct behaviour for all values 4..65535, odd and even; scenario with swept values.

rules.quote: Port: i_rst_n; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Reset (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Active-low reset
rules.statement: i_rst_n is an active-low reset whose assertion is asynchronous and whose release is synchronous to i_clk.

review.reason: Quote states async assertion, sync release, active-low; scenario check suitable.

rules.quote: Port: o_tx_ready; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Transmit stream: the transmitter can accept a byte at the next edge
rules.statement: o_tx_ready resets to 1.

review.reason: Reset value 1 stated; checkable on interface signal.

rules.quote: Port: o_tx_ready; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Transmit stream: the transmitter can accept a byte at the next edge
rules.statement: When o_tx_ready is 1 the transmitter can accept a byte on i_tx_data at the next clock edge.

review.reason: Meaning describes handshake; the transfer on a clock edge is checkable only via scenario, but actor of the acceptance is the slave (ok). The quote is a loose description of o_tx_ready; no i_tx_valid is mentioned in the port, so checkable behaviour is weak. Keep scenario but the strength is better SHOULD-less; treat as MUST scenario.

rules.quote: Port: i_tx_data; Direction: input; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Transmit stream: byte to send; bit 0 is sent first
rules.statement: Bit 0 of i_tx_data is sent first on o_txd.

review.reason: Bit order LSB first on o_txd stated; scenario appropriate.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_valid; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: the holding register holds a byte
rules.statement: o_rx_valid resets to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated.

rules.quote: Port: i_rx_ready; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: the consumer takes the held byte at this edge
rules.condition: i_rx_ready is 1 at a clock edge while o_rx_valid is 1
rules.statement: The held byte is taken by the consumer at that edge.

review.reason: Consumer takes byte at the edge; behaviour of the DUT (o_rx_valid deasserting) is not stated in the quote. Only the handshake semantics is stated; actor is the consumer (master) side.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_data; Direction: output; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: received byte; bit 0 was received first; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: o_rx_data resets to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_data; Direction: output; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: received byte; bit 0 was received first; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: Bit 0 of o_rx_data is the first bit received; o_rx_data is qualified by o_rx_valid.

review.reason: Bit order and qualification stated.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_frame_err; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: o_rx_frame_err resets to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_frame_err; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: o_rx_frame_err is 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0, and is qualified by o_rx_valid.

review.reason: Stated by the quote; requires stop-bit stimulus so scenario.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_overrun; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: One-cycle pulse: a received byte was dropped because the holding register was full
rules.statement: o_rx_overrun resets to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_overrun; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: One-cycle pulse: a received byte was dropped because the holding register was full
rules.condition: a received byte arrives while the holding register is full
rules.statement: o_rx_overrun pulses for one cycle when a received byte is dropped because the holding register is full.

review.reason: One-cycle pulse on drop stated; needs stimulus and is checkable by assertion.

rules.quote: Port: o_txd; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Serial transmit line, idle high
rules.statement: o_txd resets to 1 and is high when idle.

review.reason: Reset value 1 and idle high are stated, but the combined rule mixes reset and idle conditions; idle is not observable from interface signals alone, so scenario is needed, not assertion.

rules.quote: All flip-flops are clocked on the rising edge of i_clk. [REQ-CLK-001] All state elements of the block shall be clocked by the rising edge of i_clk only, with no other clock, no gated clock and no latch.
rules.statement: All state elements shall be clocked only by the rising edge of i_clk, with no other clock, no gated clock and no latch.

review.reason: Quote states single rising-edge clock, no gated clock or latch; structural, not simulation-checkable, so check=none is right.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-001] When i_rst_n becomes 0, every flip-flop of the block shall take its reset value at once, without waiting for an edge of i_clk.
rules.statement: Every flip-flop shall take its reset value at once, asynchronously, without waiting for an i_clk edge.

review.reason: REQ-RST-001 states asynchronous reset of all flops; scenario test (assert reset between clock edges) fits.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-002] While i_rst_n is 0, the outputs shall have these values: o_txd = 1, o_tx_ready = 1, o_rx_valid = 0, o_rx_data = 0, o_rx_frame_err = 0, o_rx_overrun = 0.
rules.statement: Outputs shall be o_txd=1, o_tx_ready=1, o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data=0, o_rx_frame_err=0, o_rx_overrun=0.

review.reason: Reset output values are checkable every cycle from interface signals.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-003] While i_rst_n is 0, no transmit byte shall be accepted, even when i_tx_valid = 1 and o_tx_ready = 1.
rules.condition: While i_rst_n is 0, even when i_tx_valid=1 and o_tx_ready=1
rules.statement: No transmit byte shall be accepted.

review.reason: Quote forbids accepting a byte during reset; checkable by assertion (o_txd stays 1) and by scenario (no frame after release).

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-004] While i_rst_n is 0, the receiver shall not detect a start bit and shall not deliver a byte.
rules.statement: The receiver shall not detect a start bit and shall not deliver a byte.

review.reason: Quote forbids start detection and byte delivery in reset; assertion on o_rx_valid plus scenario with i_rxd low.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-005] Both i_rxd synchronizer flip-flops, and any flip-flop that holds the previous synchronised line value, shall reset to 1.
rules.statement: Both i_rxd synchronizer flip-flops and any flip-flop holding the previous synchronised line value shall reset to 1.

review.reason: Quote states reset value 1 of synchronizer flops; internal state, so exercised via scenario at release.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-006] If reset is asserted during a transmission, the frame shall be abandoned: o_txd shall become 1 at once, and the rest of the frame and the byte shall not be sent after the release.
rules.statement: The frame shall be abandoned: o_txd becomes 1 at once, and the rest of the frame and byte are not sent after release.

review.reason: Quote states frame abandonment on reset mid-transmission; scenario.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-007] If reset is asserted during a reception, the partly received frame shall be discarded and shall not produce o_rx_valid, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun after the release.
rules.statement: The partly received frame shall be discarded and shall not produce o_rx_valid, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun after release.

review.reason: Quote states partial frame is discarded with no rx outputs after release; scenario.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-008] If reset is asserted while o_rx_valid = 1, the held byte shall be discarded.
rules.statement: The held byte shall be discarded.

review.reason: Quote states held byte is discarded on reset; scenario.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-009] After the release of i_rst_n, the transmitter shall be idle with o_tx_ready = 1, and it shall be able to accept a byte at the first edge after the release.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall be idle with o_tx_ready=1 and able to accept a byte at the first edge after release.

review.reason: Quote states o_tx_ready=1 and byte acceptance at first edge after release; checkable by assertion and scenario.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-010] After the release of i_rst_n, the receiver shall be idle.
rules.statement: The receiver shall be idle.

review.reason: Quote states receiver idle after release; scenario.

rules.quote: For the first edge R1 after the release, s(R1-1) shall be taken as 1 (the reset value of the synchronizer). So if s(R1) = 0, R1 is detected as T0 (Section 10.5).
rules.condition: At first edge R1 after reset release
rules.statement: The previous synchronised value s(R1-1) shall be taken as 1, so if s(R1)=0 it is detected as start bit T0.

review.reason: Quote states s(R1-1) taken as 1 so s(R1)=0 is detected as T0; scenario.

rules.quote: [REQ-GEN-001] The block shall send and receive frames in 8N1 format: a start bit of value 0, then eight data bits with the least significant bit first, then a stop bit of value 1, with no parity bit.
rules.statement: The block shall send and receive 8N1 frames: start bit 0, eight data bits LSB first, stop bit 1, no parity bit.

review.reason: Quote states the 8N1 frame format.

rules.quote: [REQ-GEN-002] The transmitter and the receiver shall work at the same time and independently.
rules.statement: The transmitter and receiver shall operate concurrently and independently.

review.reason: Stated by REQ-GEN-002.

rules.quote: No activity of one shall change the timing or the outputs of the other.
rules.statement: Activity of the transmitter shall not change the timing or outputs of the receiver, and vice versa.

review.reason: Stated by the quote's second sentence.

rules.quote: [REQ-GEN-003] Every output port shall be driven directly by a flip-flop clocked by i_clk, so there is no combinational path from any input port to any output port.
rules.statement: Every output port shall be driven directly by a flip-flop clocked by i_clk, with no combinational path from any input port to any output port.

review.reason: Structural requirement stated by the quote. It is not checkable from interface signals, so check=none is right.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-001] The transmitter shall accept a byte at an edge only when, at that edge, i_tx_valid = 1, o_tx_ready = 1 and i_rst_n = 1.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall accept a byte at an edge only when i_tx_valid = 1, o_tx_ready = 1 and i_rst_n = 1.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-001.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-002] The transmitter shall capture i_tx_data at the accepting edge E0.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall capture i_tx_data at the accepting edge E0.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-002.

rules.quote: The value of i_tx_data at any other edge shall have no effect.
rules.condition: at any edge other than the accepting edge
rules.statement: The value of i_tx_data at any edge other than the accepting edge shall have no effect.

review.reason: 'No effect' of i_tx_data at other edges cannot be asserted every cycle from interface signals. It needs a scenario that varies i_tx_data.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-003] While the transmitter is idle (no frame in progress), o_tx_ready shall be 1.
rules.condition: transmitter idle, no frame in progress
rules.statement: o_tx_ready shall be 1 while the transmitter is idle.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-003 and is checkable against a reference model.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-004] After an accepting edge E0, o_tx_ready shall be 0 in the cycles after edges E0 to E0+10N-2 inclusive.
rules.statement: o_tx_ready shall be 0 in the cycles after edges E0 to E0+10N-2 inclusive.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-004.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-005] After an accepting edge E0, o_tx_ready shall become 1 at edge E0+10N-1, which is the last cycle of the stop bit.
rules.statement: o_tx_ready shall become 1 at edge E0+10N-1, the last cycle of the stop bit.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-005.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-006] If i_tx_valid is 0 at an edge, or o_tx_ready is 0 at that edge, the transmitter shall not accept a byte and its state shall not depend on i_tx_data.
rules.condition: i_tx_valid = 0 or o_tx_ready = 0 at an edge
rules.statement: The transmitter shall not accept a byte and its state shall not depend on i_tx_data.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-006.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-007] The transmitter shall not require i_tx_valid to stay 1 until a handshake. If i_tx_valid returns to 0 before a handshake, nothing is sent.
rules.condition: i_tx_valid returns to 0 before a handshake
rules.statement: The transmitter shall not require i_tx_valid to stay 1 until a handshake; if it drops before a handshake nothing is sent.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-007.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-008] The transmitter shall hold at most one byte, the byte being sent, and shall have no transmit buffer beyond it.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall hold at most one byte, the one being sent, with no transmit buffer beyond it.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-008. It can be exercised by offering a second byte while a frame is in progress.

rules.quote: Frame bit j (j = 0 to 9) of a byte D is: bit 0 = 0 (start bit); bit j = D[j-1] for j = 1 to 8; bit 9 = 1 (stop bit). [REQ-TX-010] For a byte D accepted at edge E0, o_txd in the cycle after edge E0+k shall equal frame bit floor(k / N) of D, for every k from 0 to 10N-1.
rules.condition: byte D accepted at edge E0, for k from 0 to 10N-1
rules.statement: o_txd in the cycle after edge E0+k shall equal frame bit floor(k/N) of D (bit 0 = 0, bit j = D[j-1], bit 9 = 1).

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-010 and the frame bit definition.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-011] Each of the 10 frame bits shall be driven on o_txd for exactly N consecutive cycles.
rules.statement: Each of the 10 frame bits shall be driven on o_txd for exactly N consecutive cycles.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-011.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-012] If a new byte is accepted at edge E0+10N, its start bit shall begin at edge E0+10N, with no idle cycle between the stop bit of the previous frame and the new start bit.
rules.condition: new byte accepted at edge E0+10N
rules.statement: The start bit of the new frame shall begin at edge E0+10N with no idle cycle after the previous stop bit.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-012.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-013] If no byte is accepted at edge E0+10N, o_txd shall be 1 from edge E0+10N until the edge after which the next accepted frame starts.
rules.condition: no byte accepted at edge E0+10N
rules.statement: o_txd shall be 1 from edge E0+10N until the edge after which the next accepted frame starts.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-013.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-014] While the transmitter is idle, o_txd shall be 1.
rules.statement: o_txd shall be 1 while the transmitter is idle.

review.reason: Matches REQ-TX-014.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-001] i_rxd shall go through a synchronizer of exactly two flip-flops clocked by i_clk, with no logic between them, before any other logic of the block uses it.
rules.statement: i_rxd shall pass through a synchronizer of exactly two i_clk flip-flops with no logic between them before any other logic uses it.

review.reason: Structural requirement stated by REQ-RX-001. It is not checkable from interface signals, so check=none is right.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-002] The receiver shall be in one of two conditions, idle or receiving. It shall be idle after reset, after a glitch (REQ-RX-005) and after the stop-bit sample of a frame (REQ-RX-013).
rules.statement: The receiver shall be either idle or receiving, and shall be idle after reset, after a glitch and after the stop-bit sample of a frame.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-002.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-003] While idle, the receiver shall detect a start bit at edge T0 if and only if s(T0-1) = 1 and s(T0) = 0.
rules.statement: The receiver shall detect a start bit at edge T0 if and only if s(T0-1) = 1 and s(T0) = 0.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-003.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-004] The receiver shall not need the line to be high for longer than the single sample s(T0-1) = 1 before a start bit.
rules.statement: The receiver shall not need the line high for longer than the single sample s(T0-1) = 1.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-004.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-005] At edge T0+H the receiver shall check the start bit. If s(T0+H) = 1, the receiver shall treat the event as a glitch, return to idle and receive no byte.
rules.statement: The receiver shall check the start bit at T0+H; if s(T0+H) = 1 it shall treat it as a glitch, return to idle and receive no byte.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-005.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-006] A glitch shall not change o_rx_valid, o_rx_data or o_rx_frame_err, and it shall not make o_rx_overrun pulse.
rules.statement: A glitch shall not change o_rx_valid, o_rx_data or o_rx_frame_err and shall not make o_rx_overrun pulse.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-006.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-007] After a glitch checked at edge T0+H, the receiver shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > T0+H at which REQ-RX-003 holds.
rules.condition: after a glitch checked at T0+H
rules.statement: The receiver shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > T0+H at which the start condition s(T0'-1)=1, s(T0')=0 holds.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-007.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-008] If s(T0+H) = 0, the receiver shall go on to receive the frame.
rules.statement: The receiver shall go on to receive the frame.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-008.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-010] For a frame detected at T0 and confirmed at T0+H, the receiver shall sample data bit i (i = 0 to 7) at edge T0+H+(i+1)N. The received byte bit i shall be s(T0+H+(i+1)N).
rules.condition: frame detected at T0 and confirmed at T0+H
rules.statement: The receiver shall sample data bit i (0 to 7) at edge T0+H+(i+1)N, and received bit i shall be that sample.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-010.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-011] The receiver shall sample the stop bit at edge M = T0+H+9N.
rules.statement: The receiver shall sample the stop bit at edge M = T0+H+9N.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-011.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-012] Only the samples s(T0-1), s(T0), s(T0+H), the eight data-bit samples and s(M) shall affect the result of a frame. Values of i_rxd at all other edges between T0 and M shall be ignored.
rules.statement: Only s(T0-1), s(T0), s(T0+H), the eight data samples and s(M) shall affect a frame's result; i_rxd at other edges between T0 and M shall be ignored.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-012.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-013] Once it has sampled the stop bit at M, the receiver shall be idle.
rules.condition: after sampling the stop bit at M
rules.statement: The receiver shall be idle once it has sampled the stop bit at M.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-013.

rules.quote: It shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > M at which REQ-RX-003 holds, including T0' = M+1 when s(M) = 1 and s(M+1) = 0.
rules.statement: The receiver shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > M where the start condition holds, including T0' = M+1 when s(M) = 1 and s(M+1) = 0.

review.reason: Matches the quote's second sentence.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-014] Every frame confirmed at T0+H shall complete at M, whatever the value of s(M).
rules.statement: Every confirmed frame shall complete at M regardless of s(M).

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-014.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-015] The receiver shall keep sampling and receiving frames while a byte is waiting in the holding register. A low i_rx_ready shall not stall or delay the receiver.
rules.condition: a byte is waiting in the holding register
rules.statement: The receiver shall keep sampling and receiving frames; a low i_rx_ready shall not stall or delay it.

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-015.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-020] At the delivery edge V = M+2 of a completed frame, if o_rx_valid = 0, the block shall load the frame into the holding register. o_rx_valid then becomes 1, o_rx_data becomes the received byte and o_rx_frame_err becomes the inverse of s(M).
rules.condition: at delivery edge V = M+2 with o_rx_valid = 0
rules.statement: The block shall load the frame: o_rx_valid becomes 1, o_rx_data becomes the received byte and o_rx_frame_err becomes the inverse of s(M).

review.reason: Matches REQ-RX-020.

questions.question: docs/RTL_RULES.md is external. What does it require, so that UL-13-02 can be checked?
questions.note: The content of docs/RTL_RULES.md is not given in the documents. It is only referenced, with the revision 'current revision in the repository'. The designer must supply the rules or state how conformance is checked.

answered_questions.question: Does the receiver drop the new byte or overwrite the old one on overrun, and is o_rx_overrun a one-cycle pulse? Also when exactly is a byte 'taken' relative to the o_rx_valid/i_rx_ready handshake?
answered_questions.answer: The new byte is dropped (not overwritten); the held byte, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err stay unchanged. o_rx_overrun is 1 for exactly one cycle. A byte is taken at an edge where o_rx_valid=1, i_rx_ready=1 and i_rst_n=1.

answered_questions.question: Is the receiver's mid-bit sample point defined exactly (for example CLKS_PER_BIT/2) for odd values of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. H = floor(N/2), so for odd N it is rounded down (N=5 gives H=2).

answered_questions.question: UL-4-04 says elaboration should stop for out-of-range PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT. Is this mandatory (a SHOULD) and how is it to be verified, given that behaviour outside 4..65535 is otherwise unspecified?
answered_questions.answer: It is only a SHOULD (recommended), not mandatory. Behaviour for illegal values is not specified and not verified.

answered_questions.question: UL-4-01 gives the bit period N as exactly PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT cycles for both TX and RX. Does the receiver's sampling use HALF_BIT from the start-bit edge, and how does this behave for odd N, where H is not exactly N/2?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The start-bit check is at T0+H, where H counts edges from the detection edge T0. The data samples then follow every N edges. For odd N, H = floor(N/2), so H is not exactly N/2 and the spec defines it as the floor.

answered_questions.question: Is o_tx_ready a pure status signal? The port table lists no i_tx_valid, so how is a byte accepted on i_tx_data, and is acceptance at the next edge qualified by o_tx_ready alone?
answered_questions.answer: The port table does list i_tx_valid. A byte is accepted at an edge only when i_tx_valid=1, o_tx_ready=1 and i_rst_n=1, and i_tx_data is captured at that edge. o_tx_ready alone is not enough.

answered_questions.question: After the consumer takes the byte (i_rx_ready=1 while o_rx_valid=1), must o_rx_valid deassert on the next cycle, or can a new byte be loaded back to back?
answered_questions.answer: After a take, o_rx_valid becomes 0 at that edge unless a new byte is loaded at the same edge. A new frame delivered at V when the held byte is taken at V is loaded back to back, o_rx_valid stays 1 and there is no overrun.

answered_questions.question: Do o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err hold or clear when o_rx_valid is 0 after the byte is consumed? Both are only 'qualified by o_rx_valid'.
answered_questions.answer: They hold. While o_rx_valid=0 they keep the last loaded byte's values, or 0 if no byte has been loaded since reset. They change only on a new load or on reset.

answered_questions.question: Is reset release synchronization internal, and how long after reset release does o_tx_ready return to 1?
answered_questions.answer: Reset release synchronisation is external (ENV-001), and the block has no reset synchronizer. After release the transmitter is idle with o_tx_ready=1 and can accept a byte at the first edge after release. o_tx_ready is already 1 during reset.

answered_questions.question: o_tx_ready=1 during reset while no byte may be accepted even with i_tx_valid=1: confirm the handshake does not count as a transfer during reset, and what the scoreboard should assume.
answered_questions.answer: Confirmed. o_tx_ready=1 during reset (D-001), but a handshake needs i_rst_n=1, so no byte is accepted during reset. The scoreboard should assume that no transmit byte is accepted while i_rst_n=0.

answered_questions.question: Is reset release assumed synchronous to i_clk? 'First edge after the release' and R1 are ambiguous if i_rst_n deasserts asynchronously near a clock edge.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. Release is synchronous to i_clk, and the environment must guarantee this, meeting recovery and removal times. R1 is the first edge after the release, and s(R1-1) is taken as 1.

answered_questions.question: The quotes never give the relation between H and N, nor whether N is even or has a minimum value. Do the sample-point rules, which use T0+H, T0+H+(i+1)N and M=T0+H+9N, assume a fixed H such as N/2?
answered_questions.answer: H is fixed as floor(N/2). N must be in 4..65535 and may be odd or even.

answered_questions.question: What are the reset values and reset type (sync or async) of o_txd, o_tx_ready, the receive outputs and the two-flop synchronizer? The initial s value affects start detection s(T0-1)=1 right after reset. What happens to a frame in progress at reset, for both the transmitter and the receiver?
answered_questions.answer: Reset is asynchronous assertion. Reset values: o_txd=1, o_tx_ready=1, o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data=0, o_rx_frame_err=0, o_rx_overrun=0. Both synchronizer flops, and any flop holding the previous synchronised value, reset to 1. A transmit frame in progress is abandoned, with o_txd going to 1 at once and the byte lost. A partly received frame is discarded and gives no valid, frame-error or overrun output after release.

answered_questions.question: 'o_tx_ready becomes 1 at edge E0+10N-1' is ambiguous about whether it is visible in the cycle after that edge, and which cycle first allows acceptance. Is a back-to-back byte accepted at E0+10N, or at E0+10N-1 once o_tx_ready is already 1? Does 'o_tx_ready 0 after edges E0..E0+10N-2' conflict with this?
answered_questions.answer: o_tx_ready is 0 in the cycles after edges E0..E0+10N-2 and becomes 1 at edge E0+10N-1. It is therefore 1 in the cycle after that edge, and it is the last stop-bit cycle. A back-to-back byte is accepted at E0+10N (the next edge, as in the N=4 example: ready 1 after E0+39, handshake at E0+40). There is no conflict.

answered_questions.question: Can a new frame's delivery edge V coincide with the previous byte being taken or with the previous overrun pulse? Does the overrun (o_rx_overrun) depend on i_rst_n at V?
answered_questions.answer: V can coincide with a take of the previously held byte. In that case the new byte is loaded and there is no overrun. Two deliveries are at least H+9N+1 cycles apart, so an overrun pulse of one cycle cannot overlap the next frame's V. The reset is covered by the spec: while i_rst_n=0 the receiver delivers nothing and o_rx_overrun is 0.

answered_questions.question: If an overrun byte also has a stop bit of 0, is o_rx_frame_err suppressed entirely, and can it appear on a later byte? Confirm precisely what 'not reported' means.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. When a byte is dropped its frame-error flag is dropped with it and not reported. o_rx_frame_err keeps the held byte's value and is not affected. The flag belongs only to the dropped frame and does not carry onto a later byte.

answered_questions.question: For all-low line, is the outcome deterministic (delivery vs overrun depends on i_rx_ready/o_rx_valid)? Confirm the scenario must cover both.
answered_questions.answer: The outcome is deterministic under the Section 7.8 rules. The block delivers 0x00 with o_rx_frame_err=1, or drops it with an overrun pulse if the holding register is full and i_rx_ready=0. Only one frame is produced while the line stays low. Coverage requires frame error both delivered and dropped by overrun.

answered_questions.question: What are the exact minimum sampling margins at PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=4 (e.g. which clock within the bit the receiver samples at)? The quote gives no number to check against.
answered_questions.answer: At N=4, H=2. With an exact bit period, each sample is 2 edges after the first edge of the bit and 1 edge before its last edge. The data samples are at T0+H+(i+1)N.

answered_questions.question: Is the 65535 value verified only by elaboration and synthesis (D-012), so no simulation is expected at that value? Is 1024 the largest simulated value?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. 65535 is covered by elaboration and synthesis only and is not simulated. The simulated configurations are 16, 4, 5 and 1024, so 1024 is the largest simulated value.

answered_questions.question: i_rxd is an asynchronous input, but the rule requires it to change away from rising edges of i_clk. Does this apply only in simulation, with the synchronizer handling real asynchrony?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The rule is a simulation obligation so that s(E) is well defined. The synchronizer handles real asynchrony, and its metastability is not modelled or checked.

answered_questions.question: Is reset assertion at the start of simulation asynchronous, given that only the release is required to be synchronous?
answered_questions.answer: Reset assertion is asynchronous by design and only the release must be synchronous. ENV-002 only requires i_rst_n to be held at 0 for at least 2 cycles at the start of simulation.

answered_questions.question: What range of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT values counts as legal for the timing requirement and the counter-width limit?
answered_questions.answer: The legal range is 4 to 65535. Timing at 50 MHz must be met for every legal value, and the counters need to be at most 16 bits wide.

answered_questions.question: D-003: V = M+2 — is M the edge at which i_rxd is sampled at the pin, with the synchronizer latency already included in the sample point, or does the middle-of-bit sampling H count synchronized edges? Define the reference consistently with D-002.
answered_questions.answer: s(E) is the value of i_rxd captured by the first synchronizer flop at edge E. T0, H and M are all defined on s, so the sampling offsets count edges of s. V = M+2 is the extra two-flop synchronizer latency on the delivery side, as set by D-002 and D-003.

answered_questions.question: D-007 vs D-010: when a byte is dropped (overrun), are o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err kept unchanged? Confirm the dropped byte does not update them.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. On overrun the held byte, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err are unchanged. The dropped byte and its frame-error flag do not update them.
